methods.name: BRC consecutive-multiplier root/remainder transition
capabilities: exact fixed-N multiplier root/remainder sequence through m=100 with only one initial N-dependent root materialization
checked-in 99-entry dyadic gamma predictor table for N up to 4096 bits
exact precision specialization by right shift from one high-precision table
cached exact predictor fallback above the static cap

methods.core_law: With gamma_m=sqrt((m+1)/m)-1, choose B so J_m<2^(B-1), C_m=floor(2^B gamma_m), d0=floor(C_m J_m/2^B). Then J_(m+1)-(J_m+d0) is in {0,1,2}. The provisional remainder is R_m+N-d0(2J_m+d0); subtracting successive odd basin widths at most twice yields exactly R_(m+1).
methods.hard_boundary: Finite exact integer multiplier scan only; checked-in static performance fast path N<=4096 bits and m<=100. Larger-N predictor generation is cached but no one-off speed claim is made. Performance evidence is environment-specific constant-factor timing. No asymptotic factorization speedup, no novelty claim for multiplier-Fermat/Lehman square-gap factoring, no recovery after erasing R_m, and no Foundation promotion.

methods.name: BRC fourth-order fixed-phase lifted-moment transport
capabilities: exact unbounded odd-N mod-8 root/remainder transport from an m^7>=128N tail
cubic phase-root extrapolation from four labeled exact phase states
exact target residual using the signed remainder jet and a four-coordinate lifted quadratic moment carrier
uniform integer fourth-difference correction bound -347..7
negative correction recovery using the existing 1024-byte normalized reciprocal table with at most two estimate increments and one adjacent-candidate comparison
nineteen fixed seed-root transitions followed by recurrence with no further target square roots
moment updates whose new products use only a bounded correction or fixed small coefficients

methods.core_law: For (m+8i)N=J_i^2+R_i, i=0..3, let u=Delta J_0, v=Delta^2 J_0, w=Delta^3 J_0 and C=4J_3-6J_2+4J_1-J_0. Then (m+32)N-C^2=-R_0+4R_1-6R_2+4R_3-2(4uw+3v^2+12vw+6w^2). Under m^7>=128N, e=Delta^4J_0 lies in [-347,7]. The lifted moments UW,V2,VW,W2 update using only bounded e, and the existing Round-13 reciprocal table recovers the dominant negative correction exactly.
methods.observer_contract: Retain four labeled phase triples plus the ordered finite-difference and quadratic-moment state. A root-only, remainder-total, Boolean-support, or unlabeled phase quotient cannot reproduce the exact residual or completion-gap future operation.
methods.hard_boundary: Exact integer transport on the declared odd-N fixed-phase tail. Nineteen direct-root seeds must be amortized by a long stream. Finite timing crossover is runtime-dependent. The result does not reduce the multiplier horizon, change Lehman/Hart factorization complexity, imply RSA practicality, mutate Foundation, or create a new top-level BRC family.

methods.name: BRC square-gap quadratic-residue prefilter
capabilities: checked-in exact packed quadratic-residue tables for moduli 4032 and 20160
deterministic cached fallback table generation for arbitrary positive moduli
zero-false-negative rejection of impossible square gaps
exact integer square-root confirmation on survivors
typed separation of BRC next-square addition cost from ceiling-square Fermat completion cost
immediate square-gap witness surface for classical difference-of-squares composition
runtime benchmark surface separating gap-only second-root savings from full ceiling-gap pipeline cost
methods.core_law: If an integer value is a square then its residue modulo M belongs to the precomputed quadratic-residue table Q_M. Therefore Q_M[value mod M]=0 safely rejects squarehood before exact isqrt confirmation. For M=4032 the table has 192 live residue classes out of 4032 (1/21) and a 504-byte raw payload; for M=20160 it has 576 live classes out of 20160 (1/35) and a 2520-byte raw payload.
methods.hard_boundary: Quadratic-residue filtering, Fermat difference of squares, and Lehman-style multiplier use are classical prior art. Passing the residue filter is not a square certificate. Rejection percentage is not runtime speedup: on the checked small-integer semiprime sample direct Python isqrt was faster, while deterministic larger-integer timing showed the table becomes useful; full ceiling-gap pipeline gains were only about 1.2-1.4x in the tested big-integer ranges because ceil(sqrt(mN)) remains on the critical path. Timings are environment-dependent diagnostics, not complexity theorems. Coarse BRC basin support/Pell resonance remains unpromoted as a selector.

methods.core_law: For phase-spaced states (m+8i)N=J_i^2+R_i, let a=J_1-J_0, b=J_2-J_1 and C=3J_2-3J_1+J_0. Then (m+24)N-C^2=R_0-3R_1+3R_2-6b(b-a). On 4m^5>=N, e=J_3-C is the integer third phase difference and satisfies -3<=e<=387. For C>=75078, floor(G/(2C+1)) lies in {e,e+1}; the existing Round-13 1 KiB lower-reciprocal table recovers that floor with at most two increments, and one sign check yields the exact (J_3,R_3).
methods.observer_contract: Retain three labeled phase triples (m_i,J_i,R_i). Roots alone, Boolean support, or an unlabeled aggregate are inadequate because the exact residual and future completion-gap observer depend on the individual remainders and phase order.
methods.hard_boundary: Exact integer transport only on the already-certified odd-N order-one deep tail and fixed mod-8 representative phases. The finite performance crossover is runtime-dependent; direct division remains appropriate for smaller operands. This does not reduce the multiplier horizon, change Lehman/Hart factorization complexity, imply RSA practicality, or create a new top-level BRC family.

methods.name: BRC stride-8 quotient/remainder jet tail
capabilities: decompose the odd-N mod-8 sparse multiplier stream into five fixed-step residue orbits
seed every orbit with three exact Euclidean quotient samples, exactly fifteen divisions total
quadratically extrapolate the next quotient and recover the exact quotient/remainder by at most four signed denominator repairs
prove the quotient third-difference correction interval [-4,4] under the common linear tail and m>=962h
retain exact quotient remainder and bounded first/second finite-difference repair coordinates
avoid a fresh large-integer quotient division and generic quotient-times-denominator product after seeding
compose with the order-one linear BRC root closure and the staged square-gap residue cascade
provide an allocation-free in-place scan path for large-integer hot loops
operate without a multiplier-horizon table or upper multiplier bound
methods.core_law: For one fixed source residue class modulo 8, let q_m=floor(2hJ_m/(4m+h)) and rho_m be the exact Euclidean remainder. Consecutive visits differ by 8. Under 4m^5>=N and m>=962h, the smooth third-difference plus source-root phase has magnitude below one, while the floor phase contributes strictly between -4 and 4; hence epsilon=q_(m+8)-3q_m+3q_(m-8)-q_(m-16) lies in [-4,4]. Carrying rho and P=(Delta q+Delta^2 q)(D+32) yields the exact provisional residual S=rho+2h(J'-J)-32q-P, normalized by at most four additions/subtractions of D'=D+32. Five orbits times three samples require fifteen seed divisions; all later quotient states are exact recurrence states.
methods.hard_boundary: This extends t0.brc_linear_deep_tail and composes with t0.brc_square_gap_cascade; it is not a new top-level tool family. The proof controls exact multiplier-state transport only and does not shorten a Lehman/Hart-style search horizon or establish a factorization-complexity improvement. Finite Python benchmarks favor the jet only for sufficiently large integers (around 4096 bits in the committed environment); small-size routing should retain native division. The exact quotient remainder must not be collapsed to quotient-only or a fitted real trend.

methods.name: BRC multi-strip smooth-relation lattice / GF(2) carrier facade
capabilities: exact cross-multiplier relation extraction x^2-D=mN with shared x^2=D mod N semantics
exact B-smooth factorization carrier with full exponent and parity projections
incremental GF(2) dependency detection retaining relation provenance
exact square-congruence reconstruction and gcd witness surface

methods.core_law: Every smooth BRC lattice point x_i^2-D_i=m_i N gives x_i^2 congruent D_i mod N, so relations from different multiplier strips combine in one factor-base algebra without any condition on the product of multiplier labels. The exponent parity projection is sufficient for GF(2) dependency detection, but full exponents and x provenance must be retained to reconstruct the square congruence. Multiplier provenance may be forgotten only after relation extraction when future operations are restricted to dependency/congruence construction.
methods.hard_boundary: Dixon, QS, MPQS, SIQS, B-smooth factor-base collection, GF(2) linear algebra and congruence-of-squares factoring are classical prior art. The reference implementation uses trial division and incremental bitset elimination and is not a production sieve. Finite relation-yield/factoring-budget improvements are not asymptotic complexity results or novelty claims. The minimum-gap heap optimizes only next-gap ordering, not proved smoothness probability. No Foundation promotion is made.

methods.name: BRC square-increment finite-difference jet tail
triggers: compose quotient jet with square-gap tables
capabilities: retain exact E=q(2J+q) on each of the five fixed-step mod-8 source orbits
prove the exact third-difference product identity coupling quotient and root jets
prove the sharp common-tail root third-difference interval [-3,387]
reuse the quotient-jet intervals epsilon in [-4,4] and Delta^2 q in [-2,98]
retain the sole unbounded mixed product (Delta q)(Delta^2 J) and transport it using only bounded-coefficient multiplications
after fifteen quotient divisions and fifteen direct square-increment seed products, perform no fresh division and no multiplication of two N-growing operands
preserve exact multiplier root/remainder states with at most two ordinary BRC root corrections
compose unchanged with the BALANCED 4032/12155/12673 square-gap residue cascade
methods.core_law: On one stride-8 source orbit let s=nabla q, a=nabla^2 q, t=nabla J, u=nabla^2 J, e=nabla^3 q_new, w=nabla^3 J_new and E=q(2J+q). Then nabla^3 E_new = e(2(J+q+s+a+t+u+w)+e)+2w(q+s+a)+6(su+a(s+t)). The quotient jet gives e in [-4,4] and a in [-2,98]. For J=floor(sqrt(mN)), the common tail 4m^5>=N gives 0<Delta_8^3 sqrt(mN)<=384; floor phase contributes strictly between -4 and 4, hence w lies in the sharp integer interval [-3,387]. Retaining M=su and updating M_new=M+s w+(a+e)u+(a+e)w means every post-seed product has a fixed bounded integer factor.
methods.hard_boundary: This is an exact multiplier-state execution optimization extending t0.brc_quotient_jet_tail; it does not shorten a Lehman/Hart-style multiplier horizon, change factor-search complexity, establish RSA practicality, or create a new top-level BRC family. Finite CPython timings favor the difference jet only for sufficiently large integers (near parity at 4096 bits and favorable at 8192/16384 bits in the committed run); smaller inputs should retain the fresh native product. The exact quotient remainder, root finite differences, energy finite differences, and mixed provenance coordinate must not be collapsed.
